::: {#def-positional-invariance .theorem}
## Positional invariance

The assumption that the value of [component function](#def-separability) $g_{ti}$ is invariant under a re-ordering of network values and an identical re-ordering of network weights. i.e. $g_{ti}$ is [positionally invariant](#def-positional-invariance) with respect to $\mathscr{G}_t$ if for all $\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{X}' \in \{0,1\}^n$


$$
\mathbf{X}_{\mathcal{N}_i} = \mathbf{M}\mathbf{X}'_{\mathcal{N}_j}, 
\quad 
\Psi_{i,\mathcal{N}_i} = \mathbf{M}\Psi_{j,\mathcal{N}_j}
\Rightarrow
g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}) = g_{tj}(\mathbf{X}').
$$

An exposure mapping shows positional invariance with respect to graph set $\mathcal H = \{\mathscr{G}_t\}_{t \in [1:K]}$ if it is separable and all its component functions show positional invariance with respect to an element of  $\{\mathscr{G}_t\}_{t \in [1:K]}$. A structural equation is positionally invariant if its exposure mapping is positionally invariant. 
:::
